<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>P</c>rídie Idus Octóbris Luna quarta décima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ, via Aurélia, natális beáti Callísti Primi, Papæ et Mártyris; qui, Alexándri Imperatóris jussu, diútius fame in cárcere cruciátus, et quotídie fústibus cæsus, tandem, præcipitátus e fenéstra domus in qua custodiebátur, atque in púteum demérsus, victóriæ triúmphum proméruit.
<h>A</h>rímini sancti Gaudéntii, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
<h>C</h>æsaréæ, in Palæstína, sanctórum Carpónii, Evarísti et Prisciáni, fratrum beátæ Fortunátæ, qui, gládio iuguláti, páriter martýrii corónam percepérunt.
<h>I</h>tem sanctórum Saturníni et Lupi.
<h>C</h>æsaréæ, in Palæstína, sanctæ Fortunátæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, ac prædicatórum Mártyrum Carpónii, Evarísti et Prisciáni soróris; quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, post equúleum, ignes, béstias et ália torménta superáta, spíritum Deo réddidit. Ipsíus corpus póstea Neápolim, in Campánia, delátum fuit.
<h>T</h>udérti, in Umbria, sancti Fortunáti Epíscopi, qui (ut beátus Gregórius Papa refert) in immúndis spirítibus effugándis imménsæ grátia virtútis emícuit.
<h>H</h>erbípoli, in Germánia, sancti Burchárdi, qui fuit primus illíus civitátis Epíscopus.
<h>B</h>rugis Flandrórum sancti Donatiáni, Rheménsis Epíscopi.
<h>T</h>réviris sancti Rústici Epíscopi.
<h>L</h>ugdúni, in Gállia, sancti Justi, Epíscopi et Confessóris, miræ sanctitátis et prophétici spíritus viri; qui, Episcopátu demísso, in erémum Ægýpti, una cum Lectóre suo Viatóre, secéssit, ibíque, cum áliquot annos próximam Angelis egísset vitam, et dignus suórum labórum finis advenísset, corónam justítiæ perceptúrus migrávit ad Dóminum. Ipsíus sanctum corpus, una cum óssibus beáti Viatóris, qui ejúsdem Epíscopi fúerat miníster, Lugdúnum póstea quarto Nonas Septémbris delátum fuit.
<h>E</h>ódem die deposítio beáti Domínici Loricáti.
<h>A</h>rpíni, in Látio, sancti Bernárdi Confessóris.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.16a2ed7d5b:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>O</c>ctober 14th 2027, the 14th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, upon the Aurelian Way, the blessed martyr Pope Callistus. By command of the Emperor Alexander he was long starved in prison, and cudgelled every day, then he was cast headlong out of a window of the house wherein he was warded, and drowned in a well, and so earned the triumph of victory.
<h>A</h>t Rimini, (in the fourth century,) the holy martyr Gaudentius, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Caesarea, in Palestine, the holy martyrs Carponius, Evaristus, and Priscian, brothers of the blessed Fortunata, who were slain with the sword, and so received their crown.
<h>A</h>lso the holy martyrs Saturninus and Lupus.
<h>A</h>t Caesarea, in Palestine, the holy Virgin and martyr Fortunata. In the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian she overcame the rack, fire, beasts, and other torments, and gave up her soul to God. Her body was brought later to Naples, in Campania.
<h>A</h>t Todi, the holy Bishop Fortunatus, who, as is stated by blessed Gregory, was distinguished by the grace of an extraordinary power in driving away unclean spirits.
<h>A</h>t Wuerzburg, (in the eighth century,) holy Burchard, the first Bishop of that see.
<h>A</h>t Brugge, in Flanders, (toward the end of the fourth century,) holy Donatian, Bishop of Reims.
<h>A</h>t Trier, (in the sixth century,) holy Rusticus, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>U</h>pon the same day is commemorated at Lyon, in Gaul, (in the fourth century,) the holy Confessor Justus, Bishop (of that see,) a man of wonderful holiness of life, gifted with the spirit of prophecy he resigned his Bishopric, and withdrew himself into the desert of Egypt, along with Viator his Reader. There he led for some years a life bordering upon the life of Angels, and, when the worthy end of his labours came, departed hence to receive a crown of righteousness from the Lord. It was the 14th day of October, but it was upon the 2nd of September that his sacred body was brought to Lyon, along with the bones of his blessed servant Viator.
<h>O</h>n the same day, (in the year 1060,) deceased blessed Dominic, called Loricatus, (that is, the mail-wearer, from the coat of mail which he wore as a penance.)
<h>I</h>n Latium, the holy Confessor Bernard.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
